reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about cold spray preventing hot cracking, achieving dense bonding, and restoring mechanical properties in nickel-based superalloys, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises.
premises: Cold spray avoids melting and thus avoids hot cracking in nickel-based superalloys
Cold spray can produce a dense, metallurgically bonded deposit with refined grains
Post-deposition stress relief below melting point restores properties without inducing cracking
Repaired zone will have near-original mechanical properties under high temperature and cyclic loading
